claim: Saturated, back-calculation drives q so that u_raw settles at u + Tt·e
fix: Saturated, it drives `q` so that `u_raw` settles at `u + Tt·Ki·e`, just past the limit, and the output comes off the limit the moment the error reverses.
ver_evidence: src/library.jl:2566 q̇ = Ki·gate(e) + (ref - u_raw)/Tt, so q̇ = 0 gives u_raw = u + Tt·Ki·e. Probe '003' (PID Kp=1, Ki=0.5, Tt=1, limits ±1, r=3, y=0.5, run 40 s): u_raw = 2.25 = u + Tt·Ki·e, against u + Tt·e = 3.5. The same doc's section 11 and lqr_tracker.md section 7 write `v + Tt Ki e`.

claim: during a saturation episode the excess the integrator accumulates is Tt·e
fix: Raising `Tt` weakens the coupling, but during a saturation episode the excess the integrator accumulates is `Tt·Ki·e`, and an episode shorter than `Tt` winds up almost freely.
ver_evidence: src/library.jl:2566; the probe '003' line shows the saturated equilibrium u_raw - u = Tt·Ki·e (1.25 at Tt=1, Ki=0.5, e=2.5), not Tt·e (2.5). The excess the integrator holds over the reference scales with Ki.

claim: The hold alone beats ungated tracking at its better Tt, and the two together beat both
fix: The hold alone beats ungated tracking's peak at its better `Tt`, though it settles later, and the two together at `Tt = 0.5` beat both on peak and settling time.
ver_evidence: Probe '058' lines reproduce the table at W: hold (6.10, 32.5 s), ungated tracking Tt=2 (6.13, 25.8 s), Tt=0.5 (7.27, 55.2 s), hold and tracking Tt=2 (5.20, 26.9 s), Tt=0.5 (5.09, 22.0 s). The hold beats ungated tracking at Tt=2 on the peak only and settles 6.7 s later; at Tt=2 the pair settles later than ungated tracking (26.9 against 25.8 s). test/test_library.jl:3126-3129 checks peaks alone.

claim: the ungated tracking variant adds the tracking pole A11 = -1/Tt, with dq̇/dv = 1/Tt, to the plain PID's matrices
fix: the ungated tracking variant adds the tracking pole, `A₁₁ = -1/Tt`, with `∂q̇/∂v = 1/Tt`, and the correction's `-u_raw/Tt` also sets `A₁₂ = -Kd/(τd Tt)` and the first row of `B` to `[Ki - Kp/Tt, -Ki + (Kp + Kd/τd)/Tt]`.
ver_evidence: Probe '061/062' Hold=false, Track=true: A = [-1 -2; 0 -10], B = [-0.5 2.5 1.0; 0 10 0]. A11 = -1/Tt and ∂q̇/∂v = 1/Tt hold, but the q̇ row changes elsewhere too: A12 = -Kd/(τd·Tt) and B's first row becomes [Ki - Kp/Tt, -Ki + (Kp + Kd/τd)/Tt]; test/test_library.jl:2913-2914 pins the same matrices. The doc's sentence, after listing the plain matrices in full, reads as if only A11 and the v column differ.

claim: DiscretePID is the PID of section 7 with s = (q, yf) in place of x
fix: `DiscretePID{V, Hold, Track, Fixed}` is the PID of section 7 with `s = (q, yf, saturated)` in place of `x`, the code `saturated` being section 11's addition.
ver_evidence: src/library.jl:2693 s_init(::DiscretePID{V}) = (q = zero(V), yf = zero(V), saturated = zero(saturation_type(V))); probe '085' line prints (q = 0.0, yf = 0.0, saturated = 0). The store field was added by commit 4478f1af (increment 73 stage 1) and D-384, which section 11 of the same doc records.

claim: port sets, gate and reference rule are eleven methods, the four signal_ports arms among them, which AbstractPID carries
fix: The port sets, the gate and the reference rule are identical in both PIDs. The axis ports (`axis_ports`), the two `gated_error` arms and the three `correction_reference` arms read the axes alone and sit on `AbstractAntiWindupController{Hold, Track}`, which the LQR trackers share. With `parameters`, which fetches the nine parameters, `signal_ports`, `u_types` and `y_types` earn a supertype in the `AbstractLinearSystem` style, `AbstractPID{V, Hold, Track, Fixed}`, which carries them (section 10).
ver_evidence: Probe '081' lines: signal_ports is one method on AbstractPID (src/library.jl:2379-2380) built from axis_ports on AbstractAntiWindupController (2338-2339), not four arms; the two gated_error arms and the three correction_reference arms sit on AbstractAntiWindupController{Hold, Track} (2342-2352), shared with the LQR trackers, not on AbstractPID. Moved by commit 4478f1af ("the standby axis over ControllerBlock") and renamed by a12a8e86 (D-453).

claim: s_init is (q = zero(V), yf = zero(V)) with no keywords
fix: And `s_init` is `(q = zero(V), yf = zero(V), saturated = zero(saturation_type(V)))` with no keywords, as the continuous PID's `x_init` is `(q = zero(V), yf = zero(V))`;
ver_evidence: src/library.jl:2693 s_init(::DiscretePID{V}) = (q = zero(V), yf = zero(V), saturated = zero(saturation_type(V))); probe '085' line. Added by commit 4478f1af and D-384; section 11 of the same doc records the store field.

claim: the library's vector components are Integrator, FirstOrderLag, LimitedIntegrator, Relay, DiscreteLimitedIntegrator and RateLimiter
fix: The library's vector components, among them `Integrator`, `FirstOrderLag`, `LimitedIntegrator`, `Relay`, `DiscreteLimitedIntegrator` and `RateLimiter`, are one struct each over `V <: Union{Float64, SArray{<:Tuple, Float64}}`, with the law in broadcast form.
ver_evidence: src/library.jl: structs over V <: Union{Float64, SArray{<:Tuple, Float64}} also include Freeze (405), Delay (536), DiscreteIntegrator (598), Backlash (767), GaussianWhiteNoise (822), Step (1630), Sequence (1703), LimitedDoubleIntegrator (1999), Comparator (2229), PID (2541), DiscretePID (2677); probe '087' lines build four of them over SVector{2, Float64}. Added after the section's date, e.g. commit 1590a08f for LimitedDoubleIntegrator.

claim: Each boundary round re-decodes per event.
fix: Boundary event phase iterates to quiescence: rounds of full re-sweep → guards → handlers (declaration order, at most one firing per component per round).
ver_evidence: src/model.jl:738-779 (event_phase!): each round evaluates every guard once (_guards!, :749), fires handlers in declaration order with at most one per component per round, then re-sweeps (_round!, :777). No per-event re-decode happens. The D-020 annotation at design/log.md:920-922 records the removal (D-154).
ver_note: D-154 removed the per-event re-decode. Under log_rules.md rule 2 the fix may belong in the existing annotation rather than the Position.

claim: Each event fires at most once per boundary.
fix: each event firing at most `firing_budget` times per boundary, with further edges lost under a `FiringBudget` warning
ver_evidence: src/model.jl:752-766: an event may fire again in a later round while events.count[i] < firing_budget (default 4). Probe P2: the two toggling events of a Chatterer fire 8 times at boundary zero. The D-020 annotation at design/log.md:920-922 records the change (D-181).

ver_evidence: src/diagnostics.jl:1101-1121: the ConformanceFailure payload has no time field, and its docstring says the simulation time rides the StepError carrier (src/diagnostics.jl:245-248, field t). The D-053 annotation at design/log.md:1830-1831 records the move (D-249).

claim: The guard baseline is not captured by a checkpoint.
fix: detection bookkeeping, not model memory: not in `z`, carried by every checkpoint, the trace header included, and copied back by `restore!`
ver_evidence: src/checkpoint.jl:49 and :79: ModelState carries `prior`, and restore copies it back (src/checkpoint.jl:123-124). Probe P9: the ModelState fields include :prior, and checkpoint(sim.model).prior == Bool[1, 0]. The D-082 annotation at design/log.md:2834-2837 records the change (D-274).

Spec §12.6 (design/spec.md:10616-10617) defines the warm restart as checkpoint → restore! → run!. The D-082 annotation at design/log.md:2834-2837 records the change (D-274).

ver_evidence: src/sim.jl:1216-1221: replay is the ordinary loop with exactly one substitution. It restores the trace header as restore! does, and no boundary zero runs. src/sim.jl:2647-2651 and :2666: the drain fed by the recording is the one substitution. The D-101 annotation at design/log.md:3449-3452 records the change (D-274).

claim: A fixed step `h` divides `Δt_frame` and nothing else.
fix: A fixed-step method takes each span between two mandatory instants in the fewest equal steps `h_max` allows, and a due instant that falls inside a step ends the step there.
ver_evidence: src/frame.jl:127-142: a fixed-step method takes each span between mandatory instants in steps = ⌈units / h_max⌉ equal steps, and nothing requires h to divide Δt_frame. src/deployment.jl:357 and :368: RK4() and Heun() carry no step. The D-444 annotation at design/log.md:18690-18695 records the change (D-449).

claim: Step points lie at j·h after the frame top; the loop advances to the nearest step point, due instant or frame top.
fix: The frame tops and the due instants are the mandatory instants; the loop takes each span from one to the next in `⌈l / h_max⌉` equal steps, and every step end is a boundary.
ver_evidence: src/frame.jl:127-142: the loop advances span by span to the next mandatory instant, the frame top or the next due instant, and an interior step end's clock comes from the span's exact start (_instant). There are no step points j·h. The D-444 annotation at design/log.md:18690-18695 records the change (D-449).

claim: Frame tops, base ticks and step points are three lattices.
fix: The frame tops and the base ticks are two lattices in no required ratio, and every end of an integration step is a boundary.
ver_evidence: src/frame.jl:1-6: the frame tops and the due instants are on two lattices, and an interior step end has no position (src/frame.jl:106-107). The D-445 annotation at design/log.md:18755-18757 records the change (D-449).

claim: A step point on neither lattice comes from its frame's index and `j`.
fix: a step end inside a span comes from the span's exact start and its count `i` in the span, as the float nearest that instant
ver_evidence: src/frame.jl:139-141 and src/store.jl:197-206: an interior step end's clock is _instant(clock, origin + position, i, units, steps), the float nearest the span's exact start plus i·units/steps. There is no step-point index j. The D-445 annotations at design/log.md:18755-18764 record the change (D-449, D-456).

claim: Two instants closer than a few clock resolutions take clock values equal or out of order by an ulp.
fix: The positions stay ordered; every clock is the float nearest its instant, so no two boundaries swap, and a run whose clock cannot resolve two instants is refused ([D-450]).
ver_evidence: src/model.jl:580-584: every clock is the float nearest its instant, and rounding to nearest keeps order, so two boundaries never swap. A run whose clock cannot resolve its least gap is refused (frame! at src/frame.jl:87-90, via _last_frame). The D-445 annotation at design/log.md:18758-18760 records the change (D-450, then D-456 and D-458).

claim: An interior step end's clock is the span's start clock plus `i` times the span's exact step.
fix: Its clock is the float nearest the span's exact start plus `i` times the span's exact step, from its count `i` in the span, never accumulated.
ver_evidence: src/frame.jl:105-108 and :141, src/store.jl:196-206: the clock is _instant, the float nearest the span's exact start plus i·l/N, computed in Int128. It is not the start clock plus i float steps. The D-449 annotation at design/log.md:18943-18949 records the change (D-456).

claim: No recorded format changes; the descriptor carries no time quantity.

ver_evidence: src/descriptor.jl:57-74: the deployment body carries dt_frame, dt_base, h_max and h_min as exact rationals. Probe P10: the descriptor keys include :dt_frame, :dt_base and :h_max, and dt_frame = (num = 1, den = 10). D-467 (design/log.md:20271-20290) records the move. D-454 carries no annotation for it.

claim: The clock is exactly the nearest float below 2^53 and within two ulps of it beyond.

ver_evidence: src/store.jl:208-231: past 2^53, _nearest switches to _rounded_quotient, a long division that rounds once to nearest. Probe P7: 0 mismatches against the correctly rounded BigInt quotient in 1005 cases past 2^53. The D-456 annotation at design/log.md:19426-19430 records the change (D-458).
